$Comment: Raise one wave of adds now, with the game's own Spawn action, and tell the library a wave went
out. Reference it inside an instruction whose sensor decides when (Zc_Wave_Chain does, once per
wave), or hand it to a base script's behavior slot under a sensor of your own:
Two rows rise, measured from the script's entity toward the way it faces (north for an entity
placed unturned): NearCount of Role spread evenly across NearAngle degrees NearDistance blocks
out, and FarCount of FarRole across FarAngle degrees FarDistance blocks out. A spot that is not
open floor is skipped, so check each spot in the arena. Both rows always rise: give FarRole the
near row's role for a wave of one kind. Since they come from the Spawn action rather than a spawn
marker, a mod that scales spawned creatures scales them too.
Then Signal goes out (zc:wave, or zc:wave:<label>; the library counts it as the run's wave and
fires its signal event), and, when Moment names a FeedbackMoment, each member is shown it, with
the run's wave count so far as its wave argument (a line written Args ["wave"] reads it as {0}).

Role.Description: The creature the near row raises.

FarRole.Description: The creature the far row raises. Give it Role for a wave of one kind.

NearCount.Description: How many rise in the near row, as a [min, max] range of 1 or more.

NearAngle.Description: Degrees the near row spreads across, centred on the way the script's entity faces.

NearDistance.Description: Blocks from the script's entity to the near row.

FarCount.Description: How many rise in the far row, as a [min, max] range of 1 or more.

FarAngle.Description: Degrees the far row spreads across, centred on the way the script's entity faces.

FarDistance.Description: Blocks from the script's entity to the far row.

Signal.Description: The beat sent as the wave rises: zc:wave, or zc:wave:<label>.

Moment.Description: The FeedbackMoment each member is shown as the wave rises, carrying the run's wave count as wave. Empty shows nothing.

Actions.$Comment: After the signal, so the wave count it carries already counts this wave.
